key_insight: OPD generally trails GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP with external teachers, but efficiently recovers and consolidates capabilities from the student’s own GRPO-trained checkpoints.
engineering_relevance: Training domain specialists with GRPO and consolidating them via multi-teacher OPD can reduce total compute compared with joint GRPO training.
method: Compare reverse-KL OPD with GRPO using held-out accuracy versus training FLOPs.
Vary task difficulty, model sizes, domains, optimization choices, and teacher source.
Distill domain-specific GRPO checkpoints into one student with multi-teacher OPD.
evidence_signal: Own-checkpoint OPD recovered math accuracy with 50× fewer distillation FLOPs; multi-teacher distillation cost 5.2% and 8.0% of specialist training FLOPs for two and four domains, respectively, while the two-domain pipeline matched joint GRPO with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.
watch_item: The 50× result excludes teacher training: single-domain distillation adds total compute, and external-teacher OPD often inflates response length.
paper_title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
